Retirement income comes down to one question: does the cash coming in each month cover the bills going out? Social Security and a pension often leave a gap. Selling shares during a downturn to fill that gap locks in losses at the worst possible moment.

wedmoments.stock / Shutterstock.com

Dividend income fills the gap without forcing a sale. An $800,000 portfolio split equally, with $200,000 in each of four high-yield names, would pay the following. The total comes to more than $44,000 a year, or about $3,715.71 a month. Each yield is the forward annualized dividend divided by the delayed share price on the morning of November 6, 2026.

AT&T Locks Its Payout Through 2028

Stock #4: AT&T (NYSE:T)

Yield: 5.18%

Shares for $200,000: 9,337.1

Annual Passive Income: ~$10,364.15

AT&T runs a wireless business, consumer and business wireline (including AT&T Fiber and Internet Air), and a Latin America segment. The yield is high because AT&T is a capital-hungry incumbent. It cut its dividend after the WarnerMedia and DIRECTV spinoffs and has held it at $1.11 a year since, while spending heavily on fiber and buybacks. The shares sit at $21.42, down 9.57% this year.

For a telecom, free cash flow is the best test of dividend safety. Management targets $18B+ in 2026 and $19B+ in 2027, and has committed to keeping the $1.11 dividend through 2028. The main risk is debt. Net debt to adjusted EBITDA rose to 3.13x after the $23 billion EchoStar spectrum purchase, and management does not expect to get back to the 2.5x range until 2029.

Key Takeaways

AST SpaceMobile is down 26% in the past week, a slide that began with reports that SpaceX is in talks to buy Boost Mobile, ahead of AST's third-quarter report on Monday, Nov. 9.

AST's cash only just covers the burn analysts expect through 2028, and its new $1.3 billion Firefly engine deal comes on top.

The selloff means any new share sale raises less money per share, and AST's diluted share count has already more than doubled in two years.

The report has to show third-quarter capital spending inside guidance, Verizon's $45 million prepayment, and firm launch dates.

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS:NASDAQ) is down 26% in the past week. The slide began Nov. 2, when The Washington Post reported SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) is in talks to buy EchoStar's Boost Mobile, or use its network. That would put Starlink up against AST's partners, AT&T (T:NYSE) and Verizon (VZ:NYSE).

On Friday, AST also agreed to pay Firefly Aerospace (FLY:NASDAQ) more than $1.3 billion, partly in stock, for rocket engines.

Neither company has confirmed a Boost deal. But the Nov. 9 report, due after the close, now has to show AST can keep building without selling a lot more stock.

The cash covers the plan, with little to spare

First-half free cash flow was negative $1.00 billion. AST had pro forma cash of more than $3.7 billion at June 30, but $428 million backs a Ligado bridge loan. That leaves roughly $3.3 billion.

Analysts expect about $3.1 billion of burn from July 2026 through 2028. That's funded on paper with almost nothing to spare, and the Firefly cash comes on top.

And the burn only eases if revenue climbs like this:

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ millions, fiscal 2024-2028 (TIKR)

Analysts have already cut their 2027 estimate to $609 million, from $748 million at the end of June. That came after AST moved its target for about 45 BlueBirds in orbit from the end of 2026 to early 2027, and it has 12 up today. Another delay on Monday would push that revenue later and stretch the burn further.

AST has a habit of raising more

AST now trades at 29x forward sales, less than half its five-year average of 60x:

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS): forward (NTM) price/sales, last 5 years (TIKR)

So each new share AST sells now raises less. Management said in March and May it had "no plans to pursue additional convertible debt." Then in July, it sold $1.15 billion of convertible notes.

For investors watching AST SpaceMobile, the story right now is sharp volatility. The share price has dropped 15.22% over the last day and 52.15% over the past month, even as the 3 year total shareholder return of 631.23% points to a very large move over a longer horizon. AST SpaceMobile has already delivered a huge multi year move, then given a big chunk back in weeks. Is the real upside still in front of you, or already mostly cashed in by early believers?

Most Popular Narrative: 82% Undervalued

According to the most followed narrative on AST SpaceMobile, a fair value of $170 per share sits well above the last close of $30.20, which sets a very wide valuation gap for investors to think through.

The bull case is that AST is transitioning from technology demonstration to commercial rollout. The company reported Q1 2026 revenue of $14.7 million, reiterated 2026 revenue guidance of $150 to $200 million, and expects revenue to build sequentially through the year from gateway sales, government work, consulting, and potentially initial commercial service revenue.

See why 94 investors see AST SpaceMobile as 82% undervalued.

According to HedgeY, the narrative anchors on AST SpaceMobile moving from proofs and testing into a deployment phase with around 45 BlueBird satellites targeted in orbit by the end of 2026, carrier agreements already signed, and a capital base that was reported at roughly $3.5b in cash as of March 31, 2026. That combination feeds into an optimistic fair value estimate of $170 per share, which implies a very large gap to the current share price and underpins the 82.2% discount figure attached to the story.

The same storyline also highlights the tension here. The business is still loss making, losses have been widening over the past five years at about 59.6% per year, and ASTS is currently unprofitable with a negative return on equity of 33.83%. Analysts referenced in the statements expect earnings to grow 53.9% per year and forecast a move into profitability within three years, yet those are projections that need to be weighed against execution risk on manufacturing, launches, and commercial uptake.

AT&T, Inc. T has declined 11.8% over the past year against the Wireless National industry's growth of 95%. The stock has underperformed the Zacks Computer & Technology sector and the S&P 500's growth during this period.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

T outperform its peers like T-Mobile TMUS but underperformed Verizon VZ. T-Mobile declined 20.1% while Verizon gained 15.8% during this time period.

Key Growth Drivers for T

AT&T is benefiting from its aggressive fiber network expansion and improving wireless operations. During the third quarter, the company added a record 769,000 consumer and business Internet connections, comprising 442,000 fiber and 327,000 fixed wireless connections. It also gained 379,000 postpaid phone subscribers, while postpaid phone churn stood at 0.92%.

The company's Advanced Connectivity segment generated $29.48 billion in revenues, up 7.2% year over year. Service revenues increased 6.1% to $23.9 billion, supported by higher wireless subscriptions and broadband demand. Advanced home Internet revenues jumped 23.4% to $2.98 billion, reflecting customer additions and contributions from the acquired Lumen fiber business.

AT&T is also making steady progress in its convergence strategy, which focuses on providing wireless and broadband services to the same households. The advanced home Internet convergence rate improved to 42.8% from 42.5% in the preceding quarter. Its converged customer base expanded by approximately 350,000 during the third quarter. Such bundled relationships can strengthen customer loyalty and support recurring service revenues over time.

The acquisition of Lumen's mass-market fiber business and continued infrastructure deployment have strengthened AT&T's broadband footprint. The company reached approximately 39.7 million fiber locations by the end of the third quarter. It remains on track to surpass 40 million locations by the end of 2026 and more than 60 million by 2030. A larger fiber network offers opportunities to attract broadband subscribers and cross-sell wireless services.

AT&T's enterprise connectivity business is another growth avenue. Business fiber and advanced connectivity revenues increased 8.7% year over year to $1.99 billion in the third quarter. Growing demand for high-capacity networks, particularly from data centers and AI-related applications, could support future opportunities. AT&T's fiber infrastructure is positioned close to a substantial portion of U.S. data centers, while its connectivity relationships with AWS and Microsoft strengthen its exposure to this market.

title: Why Is EchoStar Stock Falling?

Why Is EchoStar Stock Falling?

EchoStar (ECHO) stock fell 8.8% on Thursday, November 5, 2026, dropping alongside a 4.4% decline in the S&P 500. The company issued no announcements, earnings reports or filings around the move. The drop came during a broad sell-off that pushed the Nasdaq Composite down 5.5% in the same session. What does EchoStar own, and what has management said about the market?

What EchoStar Owns: SpaceX Shares, Spectrum And Cash

On its August 3, 2026 call, management said EchoStar holds 261.8 million shares of SpaceX. It also pointed to what it called a solid spectrum position and about $14 billion to $15 billion in cash across the company. Management put the cost of shutting down the wireless network, together with its tax bill, at $5 billion to $7 billion. Management said on the same call that a lot of the company's value is based on SpaceX, and that it was cautious on the market because the market was at historical highs on almost every measure.

That cash is visible on the balance sheet. At September 30, 2026, EchoStar held $13.97 billion in cash and short-term investments, against $9.67 billion of debt. Beyond those holdings, management said the traditional video business continues to throw off cash, while Boost, its wireless business, lost subscribers in the June quarter.

Cash on hand matters more when markets crack. It's rule one of investing for a crash and a rally.

Did EchoStar Fall With Telecom Stocks Or The Market?

EchoStar declined alongside the broader market rather than telecom stocks, falling twice as far as the S&P 500. XLC, the SPDR fund for its Communication Services sector, slipped 0.6% that session. Among the companies on its Trefis peer list, Verizon Communications dipped 0.1% and Charter Communications rose 4.7%.

Where Does EchoStar Stock Stand After The Fall?

EchoStar has fallen this hard before. Three sessions in the prior year brought declines at least as large, the latest an 11.0% drop on June 12, 2026.

Over the past twelve months the stock returned 22.4%, against 9.9% for the S&P 500. During that year, the shares closed as low as $66.93 on November 17, 2025, and as high as $141.80 on May 20, 2026. They have lost 26.7% over the past six months, while the S&P 500 gained 0.8%.

EchoStar trades at 2.1 times its sales over the past twelve months, against 3.2 times for the S&P 500. While that multiple uses a full year of sales, revenue in the latest quarter, ended September 30, 2026, was $1.13 billion, down 68.8% from a year earlier.

Bull of the Day:

Amphenol Corporation, a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), just delivered one of the most impressive quarters any component supplier has produced in this cycle.

The connector and interconnect specialist crossed $10 billion in quarterly sales for the first time in its history, and it did so while orders nearly doubled. For a company founded in 1932, that is a remarkable late-career acceleration.

What makes Amphenol worth your attention is that it offers exposure to the artificial intelligence buildout without requiring you to pick which chip architecture wins. Every accelerator, every rack and every data center needs interconnect. Amphenol sells it to all of them.

Amphenol is part of the Zacks Electronics – Connectors industry group, which currently ranks in the top 5% out of approximately 250 Zacks Ranked Industries. Because it is ranked in the top half of all Zacks Ranked Industries, we expect this group to outperform over the next 3 to 6 months.

Take note of the favorable characteristics for this group below. Stocks in this industry are projected to experience above-average earnings growth, which is one of the most reliable precursors to higher stock prices over time.

Historical research studies suggest that approximately half of a stock's price appreciation is due to its industry grouping. In fact, the top 50% of Zacks Ranked Industries outperforms the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

It's no secret that investing in stocks that are part of leading industry groups can give us a leg up relative to the market. By focusing on leading stocks within the top 50% of Zacks Ranked Industries, we can dramatically improve our stock-picking success.

Company Description

Amphenol designs, manufactures and markets electrical, electronic and fiber optic connectors, interconnect systems, antennas, sensors and coaxial cable. Its products reach an unusually broad set of end markets: communications infrastructure, data centers, automotive, commercial aerospace, defense, industrial and mobile devices. The company is headquartered in Wallingford, Connecticut.

That breadth is the structural argument. Amphenol operates through a decentralized model of more than one hundred general managers who run their businesses with considerable autonomy. It is an unusual structure for a company of this scale, and it has produced a long record of successful bolt-on acquisitions that larger, more centralized competitors have struggled to replicate.

With small revenue and heavy cash burn, AST falls hard when investors pull back from risk.

AT&T, AST's lead U.S. carrier partner, needs its satellites in orbit, and the Nov. 9 report will test AST's launch plans.

AST SpaceMobile (ASTS:NASDAQ) fell 15% today, on the same morning it announced a U.S. Space Force contract.

A sell-off in AI and chip stocks sent the Nasdaq-100's QQQ down 6% on fears for the US data-center buildout after Democrats swept Congress on Tuesday.

AST's slide also reaches AT&T (T:NYSE), its lead U.S. carrier partner.

Rocket Lab didn't escape either

Rocket Lab (RKLB:NASDAQ) fell 12% with no news of its own. Its second-quarter revenue rose 62% from a year earlier to $234.1 million, but Neutron's first launch slipped into 2027 on Oct. 14. Both companies report after the close on Nov. 9. Can a Neutron date set Rocket Lab apart?

AT&T has a stake in the schedule

AT&T's core business is steady: postpaid phone churn held at 0.92% in the third quarter. The Washington Post reported this week that SpaceX is in talks to buy EchoStar's Boost Mobile, and that AT&T, which leases capacity to Boost, may need to approve any transfer of those leases. Will AST's report give AT&T launch dates to sell against Starlink?

What's next for AST

Until AST launches on schedule, I'd expect it to trade on investors' appetite for risk.

Tutor Perini reported third quarter 2026 revenue of US$1,720.26 million and net income of US$20.7 million, with basic earnings per share from continuing operations of US$0.39. The company also raised full year adjusted EPS guidance to a range of US$5.90 to US$6.10 and reported record operating cash flow of US$331 million.

The construction group reported a near record backlog of about US$20.4 billion with nine mega projects, supported by strong project execution and a net cash position in which cash exceeded total debt by US$707 million. This position gives management room to focus on higher margin work and ongoing risk control.

We will look at how Tutor Perini's investment narrative is affected by record quarterly revenue and raised full year earnings guidance.

Scan for other construction and infrastructure stocks showing strong order books and solid cash generation by jumping into our hand picked list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals (24 results) alongside Tutor Perini's latest earnings beat.

Tutor Perini Investment Narrative Recap

To own Tutor Perini, you need to be comfortable with a construction business built around very large, complex projects and a record backlog that can support multi year activity. The recent quarter, with US$1,720.26 million in sales and US$20.7 million in net income, supports that view by showing the order book is converting into revenue and profit.

The key short term swing factor is still execution quality on those mega projects, because delays or disputes can quickly pressure margins and earnings. Legacy contract and litigation risks do not disappear just because one quarter looks cleaner, so the raised adjusted EPS guidance mainly strengthens confidence rather than changing the core risk profile.

One announcement that ties directly to this earnings result is the updated full year adjusted EPS guidance of US$5.90 to US$6.10 per share. That range reflects management's view that current project execution, record operating cash flow of US$331 million and the near record US$20.4 billion backlog are all contributing to a stronger earnings run rate.

For you as a shareholder, that guidance matters because it sits on top of a net cash position where cash exceeds total debt by US$707 million. A balance sheet in that shape can support working capital needs on mega projects and gives the firm more flexibility if any cost overruns, legal issues or timing delays on public contracts occur again.

Tutor Perini's narrative projects US$7.6b revenue and US$483.9 million earnings by 2029. This implies 10.2% yearly revenue growth and earnings rising by about US$405.8 million from US$78.1 million today.
